question: What is the main difference between disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization is cheaper and faster than chemical disinfection.
options.B: Disinfection does not reliably kill all bacterial endospores.
options.C: Sterilization can be performed simply by wiping with soap.
options.D: Disinfection is only used for human skin and mucous membranes.

explanation: While sterilization achieves zero microbial life including tough spores, disinfection reduces pathogen loads without guaranteeing spore destruction. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h3)

question: A midwife needs to process vaginal speculums that touch mucous membranes but do not penetrate sterile tissue. Which level of processing is required?

options.A: Dry heat sterilization
options.B: Low-level disinfection
options.C: Standard hand washing
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Semi-critical items like speculums touch mucous membranes and require high-level disinfection as a minimum standard when sterilization is unavailable. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the best and most reliable method for sterilizing surgical metal instruments?

options.A: Boiling in an open pot of water for ten minutes
options.B: Autoclaving using steam under pressure
options.C: Wiping thoroughly with liquid bleach solution
options.D: Exposing the instruments to direct sunlight

explanation: Steam under pressure penetrates packs efficiently and destroys all microbial life and spores reliably. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why does boiling metal instruments in water fail to achieve true sterilization?

options.A: Boiling temperature is too high and melts the metallic handles of scissors.
options.B: Boiling water at normal atmospheric pressure does not reliably destroy bacterial endospores.
options.C: Microorganisms grow faster while the water is cooling down in the pot.
options.D: Water molecules prevent heat from reaching the inside of jointed instruments.

explanation: Standard boiling reaches only 100°C, which kills vegetative cells but leaves hardy bacterial spores alive, making it high-level disinfection at best. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which factor can seriously reduce how well a chemical disinfectant works on a surface?

options.A: Using a clean plastic container to hold the solution
options.B: Applying the liquid at room temperature
options.C: Presence of organic matter like blood or mucus
options.D: Storing the chemical stock bottle in a dark cupboard

explanation: Organic material acts as a physical shield and deactivates many chemical disinfectants, which is why thorough pre-cleaning is mandatory. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h5)

question: A midwife needs to quickly wipe down a clean stainless steel trolley between patients. Which agent is best for this non-critical surface?

options.A: Molten dry heat powder
options.B: 70% Alcohol solution
options.C: Glutaraldehyde solution
options.D: Concentrated chlorine crystals

explanation: Alcohol acts quickly on non-critical hard surfaces for routine quick wiping, whereas glutaraldehyde is toxic and reserved for immersion of delicate medical devices. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first step to take immediately after using surgical instruments during a delivery?

options.A: Scrubbing vigorously with a wire brush and soap
options.B: Decontamination by soaking in a chlorine solution
options.C: Placing them directly into a hot dry heat oven
options.D: Wrapping the tools tightly in brown paper parcels

explanation: Immediate soaking inactivates blood-borne pathogens and protects staff from accidental injuries before washing begins. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why is physical cleaning with water and detergent mandatory BEFORE putting instruments into an autoclave?

options.A: Dried organic matter protects underlying microbes from steam penetration.
options.B: Water helps the autoclave heat up faster and saves electricity.
options.C: Soap makes the metal instruments look shiny and attractive to doctors.
options.D: Detergents are powerful enough to kill bacterial spores on their own.

explanation: If blood and tissue debris remain baked on the instrument, steam cannot reach the covered microbes, resulting in failed sterilization. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which monitoring method uses heat-resistant bacterial spores to check that an autoclave is working correctly?

options.A: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.B: Chemical indicator tape
options.C: Visual inspection of shine
options.D: Biological indicators

explanation: Biological indicators contain actual hardy spores that test the true microbial-killing capability of the sterilization cycle. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h7)

question: What does a color change on a chemical indicator strip inside a surgical pack actually confirm?

options.A: The pack was exposed to specific physical conditions like heat or steam.
options.B: The autoclave machine has passed its annual engineering service.
options.C: The instruments inside have been scrubbed clean of blood stains.
options.D: Every single bacterium and spore inside the pack is definitely dead.

explanation: Chemical indicators react to physical parameters like temperature and steam exposure, confirming the item went through a cycle, though not guaranteeing absolute sterility. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of infection control in the obstetric theatre?

options.A: To speed up the turnover time between surgical procedures
options.B: To break the chain of infection by eliminating pathogens
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital-acquired drugs
options.D: To ensure compliance with hospital administrative audits

explanation: Infection control focuses on stopping harmful germs from reaching the mother or baby during surgery. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h1)

question: Who holds responsibility for maintaining safety in the obstetric operating theatre?

options.A: The sterile supply department technicians alone
options.B: The hospital infection control manager exclusively
options.C: Only the consultant obstetrician on duty
options.D: Every member of the surgical team

explanation: Theatre safety requires active vigilance and participation from all healthcare staff present in the room. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h1)

question: How does aseptic technique differ from general medical asepsis?

options.A: It allows the presence of non-pathogenic bacteria on instruments
options.B: It strives for an environment free of all pathogens and spores
options.C: It is only used outside the operating room environment
options.D: It focuses exclusively on handwashing with plain soap and water

explanation: Aseptic technique aims for total absence of living microorganisms, whereas medical asepsis only reduces their numbers. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h2)

question: When must a midwife strictly apply aseptic techniques in obstetric care?

options.A: Only when cleaning the general walls of the labour ward
options.B: During procedures like caesarean sections and catheterizations
options.C: During daily ward rounds when talking to stable patients
options.D: Whenever performing routine antenatal abdominal palpation

explanation: Invasive procedures that breach natural body barriers require strict asepsis to prevent infection. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which processing method destroys all microbial life including bacterial spores?

options.A: Sanitization
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Decontamination

explanation: Sterilization is the only process among the three that guarantees the total destruction of resistant spores. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of the initial decontamination step for surgical instruments?

options.A: To remove organic matter and blood so subsequent steps work effectively
options.B: To achieve complete sterilization before the instruments are autoclaved
options.C: To dry out moisture and prevent corrosion of metal joints
options.D: To replace chemical disinfectants with plain tap water rinsing

explanation: Cleaning away blood and tissue debris prevents organic matter from shielding microorganisms during sterilization. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the standard physical method used for steam sterilization in hospitals?

options.A: Autoclaving using moist heat under pressure
options.B: Dry heat baking in a standard kitchen oven
options.C: Boiling instruments in open water for ten minutes
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation exposure in a closed box

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to effectively kill all forms of microbial life on medical equipment. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h4)

question: How can a midwife quickly check if a wrapped instrument tray has been through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: By looking at the colour change on the external chemical indicator tape
options.B: By checking the weight of the metal container on a weighing scale
options.C: By smelling the interior wrapping paper for a distinct chemical scent
options.D: By feeling the temperature of the metallic package with bare hands

explanation: Chemical indicator tape changes colour when exposed to the proper sterilization heat parameters. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h4)

question: In what direction should a midwife scrub their arms during a surgical scrub?

options.A: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.B: In a random circular motion over the hands
options.C: Starting directly at the middle of the forearm
options.D: From the elbows down toward the fingertips

explanation: Scrubbing from the cleanest area (fingertips) to the less clean area (elbows) prevents dirty water from flowing back onto the hands. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why must hands remain elevated above the elbows after a surgical scrub?

options.A: To prevent water and contaminants from flowing downward from the arms
options.B: To make it easier for the circulating nurse to tie the back gown strings
options.C: To allow the surgical gown to slip on much faster without friction
options.D: To keep the skin cool and reduce sweating inside the sterile gloves

explanation: Gravity would pull contaminated rinse water from the forearms back down onto the surgically clean fingers if hands were lowered. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h5)

question: How should a midwife react to a sterile drape that has become wet during an operation?

options.A: Cover the wet spot with an extra layer of dry sterile gauze
options.B: Leave it alone since moisture has no effect on sterile boundaries
options.C: Dry the wet area quickly with a clean unsterile theatre towel
options.D: Treat it as contaminated because moisture permits bacterial strike-through

explanation: Wet drapes allow liquids and bacteria to pass through from underneath, breaking the sterile barrier. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the correct movement protocol when working around an established sterile field?

options.A: Reach across the sterile table whenever you need an extra instrument
options.B: Always face the field and never turn your back on it
options.C: Walk quickly around the room with your back turned to save time
options.D: Keep your arms lowered below your waistline at all times

explanation: Turning your back on a sterile field risks accidental contamination from unsterile parts of your gown. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common source of contamination in the operating theatre?

options.A: Air currents stirred up by excessive staff movement
options.B: Unsterile items touching the edges of a sterile table
options.C: Punctured surgical gloves unnoticed by the wearer
options.D: Using sterile instruments well within their expiry date

explanation: Properly sterilized instruments kept within date are safe and do not cause contamination. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h7)

question: What should a midwife do immediately upon noticing a colleague break sterile technique?

options.A: Document the error in the nursing notes without telling the surgeon
options.B: Wait until the operation finishes and report the incident in private
options.C: Ignore the mistake if the senior doctor was the one who made it
options.D: Speak up immediately to correct the breach and protect the patient

explanation: Patient safety comes first, and breaches must be addressed immediately to prevent surgical site infections. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is another common name for hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Idiopathic infections
options.B: Congenital infections
options.C: Nosocomial infections
options.D: Zoonotic infections

explanation: Nosocomial infections is the medical term used specifically for infections picked up by a patient while admitted inside a healthcare facility. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h1)

question: When do symptoms of a true hospital-acquired infection typically begin to show?

options.A: Exactly seven days after discharge
options.B: Within the first two hours of arrival
options.C: At least 48 hours after admission
options.D: Before the patient enters the ward

explanation: The 48-hour window helps clinicians confirm that the patient caught the germ inside the hospital rather than carrying it in from the community. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which type of nosocomial infection is most directly linked to the use of an indwelling urethral tube?

options.A: Surgical Site Infection
options.B: Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection
options.C: Primary Bloodstream Infection
options.D: Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia

explanation: Any infection of the urinary tract related to a catheter in place is classified specifically as a CAUTI. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: What time frame defines a surgical site infection after an operation?

options.A: Only while the patient is sleeping
options.B: Within 12 hours of the surgery
options.C: Up to 30 days post-operative
options.D: After exactly six months of healing

explanation: An infection is classified as a surgical site infection if it develops around the incision within thirty days after the procedure. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the single most common route for spreading hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Direct insect bites from house flies
options.B: Drinking untreated municipal tap water
options.C: Contact transmission via hands or equipment
options.D: Inhaling outdoor dust storms near wards

explanation: Healthcare workers moving from patient to patient with unwashed hands remain the leading pathway for spreading hospital germs. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why do hospital pathogens pose a greater treatment challenge than community strains?

options.A: They are completely invisible to standard microscopes
options.B: They multiply exclusively at freezing temperatures
options.C: They frequently show resistance to common antibiotics
options.D: They can only survive inside metal surgical trays

explanation: Constant exposure to drugs in hospitals helps select for hardy, resistant bacterial strains that standard medications cannot easily kill. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which physiological feature makes newborn babies especially prone to hospital infections?

options.A: Immature immune systems and fragile skin barriers
options.B: An excessive amount of natural body fat
options.C: Higher than normal adult body temperature
options.D: A complete absence of blood circulation

explanation: Newborns have not yet developed fully mature immune defenses, making it easy for hospital bacteria to invade through their delicate skin. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which postpartum patient faces the highest risk for developing a direct surgical site infection?

options.A: A mother who experienced a spontaneous birth
options.B: A healthy mother discharged after six hours
options.C: An antenatal client waiting for her scan
options.D: A mother recovering from a caesarean section

explanation: Surgical incisions break the protective skin barrier, creating a primary entry route for pathogens compared to an intact perineum after normal birth. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of hospital infection surveillance systems?

options.A: To collect and analyze data for detecting outbreaks
options.B: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.C: To calculate daily patient feeding budgets
options.D: To design new advertisements for the maternity wing

explanation: Surveillance is designed to track infection trends and spot unusual clusters of disease early so action can be taken. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful clinical sign of infection for a midwife to document and report?

options.A: Normal baseline temperature and pink lochia
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Purulent discharge oozing from a C-section wound
options.D: Persistent unexplained fever on the third day

explanation: Normal vital signs and standard healing processes do not indicate an infection and require no special reporting. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure for preventing hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Changing bed sheets weekly
options.C: Wearing heavy wool gloves
options.D: Painting ward walls white

explanation: Cleaning hands before and after touching patients stops germs from transferring between beds and is the baseline of infection control. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is proper waste segregation using color-coded bins important in a maternity ward?

options.A: It helps patients identify which doctor is on duty
options.B: It ensures that waste decomposes faster in the sun
options.C: It prevents accidental needle-stick injuries and contamination
options.D: It lowers the monthly electricity bill for the hospital

explanation: Separating sharps and infectious waste protects both healthcare workers and sanitation staff from accidental injury and dangerous exposure. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of infection control in a midwifery clinical setting?

options.A: To completely eliminate all bacteria from the hospital environment
options.B: To ensure that laboratory tests are processed much faster
options.C: To break the chain of transmission and protect mothers and babies
options.D: To reduce the cost of purchasing expensive hospital detergents

explanation: Infection control measures are specifically designed to interrupt how germs spread so that vulnerable patients and staff stay safe. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why are postpartum mothers and neonates considered especially vulnerable to hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: They have developing or recovering immune systems and open wounds
options.B: They are always allergic to standard hospital cleaning agents
options.C: They consume a specialized diet that attracts microorganisms
options.D: They spend more time visiting the laboratory department

explanation: Fresh surgical sites like episiotomies or cesarean sections, combined with immature or recovering immunity, make new mothers and babies prime targets for infections. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h1)

question: When should a midwife apply standard precautions during clinical duties?

options.A: Whenever hospital management is conducting an inspection
options.B: Only when caring for patients diagnosed with HIV or hepatitis
options.C: During every patient interaction regardless of diagnosis
options.D: Exclusively when assisting with complicated surgical deliveries

explanation: Standard precautions are universal, meaning they protect you and the patient during every single clinical encounter, no matter the recorded diagnosis. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which body fluid is generally excluded from the handling assumptions of standard precautions?

options.A: Amniotic fluid
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Vaginal secretions
options.D: Normal human sweat

explanation: Sweat does not contain significant bloodborne pathogens and is excluded from standard precaution assumptions unless visibly contaminated with blood. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is acknowledged as the single most effective action to stop the spread of hospital infections?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Spraying the delivery couch with bleach
options.C: Proper hand hygiene
options.D: Taking prophylactic antibiotics weekly

explanation: Cleaning hands correctly removes transient microorganisms picked up from patients and environments, stopping cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h3)

question: A midwife finishes conducting a clean vaginal examination on a stable antenatal patient. What should she do next regarding her gloves?

options.A: Keep the same gloves on but wipe them down with an alcohol swab
options.B: Remove the gloves carefully, perform hand hygiene, and put on new ones for the next patient
options.C: Remove the gloves without washing hands since no blood was visible
options.D: Wash the gloved hands thoroughly with soap and water to reuse them

explanation: Gloves are single-use items; they must be discarded between patients, followed immediately by hand hygiene to ensure complete safety. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h3)

question: What dangerous habit must midwives avoid when handling used hypodermic needles?

options.A: Carrying them on a kidney dish to the disposal point
options.B: Using a single-handed scoop technique if recapping is required
options.C: Dropping them directly into a nearby puncture-resistant box
options.D: Recapping needles using a traditional two-handed method

explanation: Two-handed recapping is a primary cause of accidental needle-stick injuries because the hand holding the cap is directly in the path of the needle point. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h4)

question: Where should the safety box for sharp objects ideally be positioned during a busy labor ward shift?

options.A: Underneath the patient's bed away from active clinical traffic
options.B: Inside the main utility room down the hospital corridor
options.C: Right at the point of use close to where the procedure occurs
options.D: Locked inside the senior midwife's office desk drawer

explanation: Placing sharps boxes close to where injections and procedures happen prevents midwives from carrying exposed needles across the room. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which group of people is NOT directly at risk when healthcare waste is managed poorly?

options.A: Community waste scavengers looking through bins
options.B: Trained astronauts orbiting in outer space
options.C: Patients recovering in the postnatal ward
options.D: Midwives and hospital cleaning personnel

explanation: Astronauts are completely isolated from terrestrial healthcare waste facilities, whereas local staff, patients, and community handlers face immediate risks. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is it unacceptable to mix infectious clinical waste with ordinary domestic rubbish?

options.A: It spreads dangerous pathogens to waste handlers and the public
options.B: It causes all hospital waste bins to change their designated color
options.C: It makes the general rubbish too heavy for the cleaners to lift
options.D: It prevents the municipal council from recycling plastic water bottles

explanation: Mixing infectious waste contaminates the entire batch, putting sanitation workers and scavengers at high risk of contracting severe infections. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which color of waste receptacle is internationally standard for collecting infectious clinical items like blood-soaked gauze?

options.A: Plain black
options.B: Bright yellow
options.C: Transparent clear
options.D: Dark brown

explanation: Yellow bins and liners are universally designated for infectious items that require special handling and treatment before final disposal. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h6)

question: A midwife assists in delivering a baby and handling the placenta. Into which container should the placenta be discarded?

options.A: An open cardboard box placed beside the delivery table
options.B: A brown container meant for pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: A yellow infectious waste bin or designated bag
options.D: A black general waste bin for domestic trash

explanation: Anatomical waste like the placenta is biological and infectious, requiring disposal in yellow containers meant for clinical waste. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is a primary treatment method used to render infectious medical waste harmless before final burial?

options.A: Compressing the waste into small metal blocks
options.B: Incineration or high-pressure autoclaving
options.C: Washing the waste items in cold river water
options.D: Leaving the bags exposed to direct sunlight

explanation: Incineration and autoclaving use extreme heat or steam pressure to effectively destroy pathogens present in medical waste. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why should waste collection bins and bags never be packed tightly to the very brim?

options.A: Overfilling makes it difficult to tie them securely and increases tear risks
options.B: Patients will complain about the aesthetic appearance of the ward
options.C: The municipal transport truck charges extra money for heavy loads
options.D: Full bags consume too much electrical power inside the incinerator

question: What immediate first aid action should a midwife take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Suck the puncture site vigorously to draw out contaminated blood

question: Why is prompt reporting of an occupational exposure incident critical for the affected midwife?
